"""Load data/financials.xlsx and compute the investor-update metrics.

Single source of truth for every number that reaches the model and the deck.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

import openpyxl

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SRC = ROOT / "data" / "financials.xlsx"
START_ACTIVE = 120
COLUMNS = ("month", "mrr", "new_customers", "churned_customers",
           "cogs", "sales_marketing_spend", "headcount")


@dataclass
class Row:
    month: str
    mrr: float
    new_customers: int
    churned_customers: int
    cogs: float
    sales_marketing_spend: float
    headcount: int
    active: int = 0
    gross_margin: float = 0.0
    churn: float = 0.0


def load_rows() -> list[Row]:
    ws = openpyxl.load_workbook(SRC, data_only=True)["raw"]
    values = list(ws.iter_rows(values_only=True))
    header = tuple(str(c).strip() for c in values[0])
    if header != COLUMNS:
        raise ValueError(f"unexpected header: {header}")
    rows = [Row(*r) for r in values[1:] if r[0] is not None]
    if len(rows) != 36:
        raise ValueError(f"expected 36 monthly rows, got {len(rows)}")
    return rows


def enrich(rows: list[Row]) -> list[Row]:
    """Fill active customers, gross margin and monthly churn in place."""
    prev_active = START_ACTIVE
    for row in rows:
        row.active = prev_active + row.new_customers - row.churned_customers
        row.gross_margin = (row.mrr - row.cogs) / row.mrr
        row.churn = row.churned_customers / prev_active
        prev_active = row.active
    return rows


def summary(rows: list[Row]) -> dict[str, float]:
    last12 = rows[-12:]
    last = rows[-1]
    cac = (sum(r.sales_marketing_spend for r in last12)
           / sum(r.new_customers for r in last12))
    arpa = last.mrr / last.active
    avg_gm = sum(r.gross_margin for r in last12) / 12
    avg_churn = sum(r.churn for r in last12) / 12
    ltv = arpa * avg_gm / avg_churn
    payback = cac / (arpa * avg_gm)
    return {
        "cac": cac,
        "arpa": arpa,
        "avg_gross_margin_12m": avg_gm,
        "avg_monthly_churn_12m": avg_churn,
        "ltv": ltv,
        "ltv_cac": ltv / cac,
        "cac_payback_months": payback,
        "revenue_year0": sum(r.mrr for r in last12),
        "sm_spend_12m": sum(r.sales_marketing_spend for r in last12),
        "new_customers_12m": sum(r.new_customers for r in last12),
        "active_last": last.active,
        "mrr_last": last.mrr,
        "arr_last": last.mrr * 12,
        "gm_last": last.gross_margin,
        "headcount_last": last.headcount,
        "first_month": rows[0].month,
        "last_month": last.month,
        "first_12m_window": last12[0].month,
    }


def load() -> tuple[list[Row], dict[str, float]]:
    rows = enrich(load_rows())
    return rows, summary(rows)

"""Build out/model.xlsx: raw data + unit economics, DCF and loan sheets.

Every derived cell is a live Excel formula; no computed values are pasted in.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from openpyxl import Workbook
from openpyxl.styles import Alignment, Border, Font, PatternFill, Side
from openpyxl.utils import get_column_letter

from metrics import ROOT, START_ACTIVE, load_rows

OUT = ROOT / "out" / "model.xlsx"
MONEY, PCT, NUM = '#,##0.00', '0.00%', '#,##0.0000'
HEAD = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="1F3864")
BAND = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="EDF1F8")
THIN = Border(bottom=Side("thin", color="B4C2DC"))
FIRST, LAST = 2, 37          # raw data rows
W12 = 26                     # first row of the trailing-12-month window


def _header(ws, row: int, labels: list[str], width: dict[str, int] | None = None):
    for i, label in enumerate(labels, start=1):
        c = ws.cell(row=row, column=i, value=label)
        c.font = Font(bold=True, color="FFFFFF")
        c.fill = HEAD
        c.alignment = Alignment(horizontal="center", vertical="center", wrap_text=True)
    for col, w in (width or {}).items():
        ws.column_dimensions[col].width = w


def _title(ws, text: str):
    c = ws.cell(row=1, column=1, value=text)
    c.font = Font(bold=True, size=13, color="1F3864")


def _label(ws, row: int, text: str, formula, fmt: str | None = None, bold=False):
    a = ws.cell(row=row, column=1, value=text)
    a.font = Font(bold=bold)
    b = ws.cell(row=row, column=2, value=formula)
    b.font = Font(bold=bold)
    if fmt:
        b.number_format = fmt
    return b


def build_raw(wb: Workbook, rows):
    ws = wb.create_sheet("raw")
    _header(ws, 1, ["month", "mrr", "new_customers", "churned_customers",
                    "cogs", "sales_marketing_spend", "headcount"],
            {"A": 11, "B": 13, "C": 16, "D": 20, "E": 13, "F": 22, "G": 11})
    for r in rows:
        ws.append([r.month, r.mrr, r.new_customers, r.churned_customers,
                   r.cogs, r.sales_marketing_spend, r.headcount])
    for row in ws.iter_rows(min_row=FIRST, max_row=LAST):
        for c in row[1:]:
            c.number_format = MONEY if c.column in (2, 5, 6) else "#,##0"
    ws.freeze_panes = "A2"


def build_unit_economics(wb: Workbook):
    ws = wb.create_sheet("unit_economics")
    _header(ws, 1, ["month", "mrr", "new_customers", "churned_customers",
                    "sales_marketing_spend", "active_customers", "gross_margin",
                    "monthly_churn"],
            {"A": 11, "B": 13, "C": 16, "D": 20, "E": 22, "F": 17, "G": 13, "H": 14})
    ws["J1"], ws["K1"] = "Input", START_ACTIVE
    ws["J1"].font = Font(bold=True, color="1F3864")
    ws["J2"], ws["K2"] = "Starting active customers (before month 1)", START_ACTIVE
    ws["J1"].value = "Inputs"
    ws.column_dimensions["J"].width = 42
    ws.column_dimensions["K"].width = 14

    for r in range(FIRST, LAST + 1):
        prev = "$K$2" if r == FIRST else f"F{r - 1}"
        ws.cell(row=r, column=1, value=f"=raw!A{r}")
        ws.cell(row=r, column=2, value=f"=raw!B{r}").number_format = MONEY
        ws.cell(row=r, column=3, value=f"=raw!C{r}")
        ws.cell(row=r, column=4, value=f"=raw!D{r}")
        ws.cell(row=r, column=5, value=f"=raw!F{r}").number_format = MONEY
        ws.cell(row=r, column=6, value=f"={prev}+raw!C{r}-raw!D{r}").number_format = "#,##0"
        ws.cell(row=r, column=7, value=f"=(raw!B{r}-raw!E{r})/raw!B{r}").number_format = PCT
        ws.cell(row=r, column=8, value=f"=raw!D{r}/{prev}").number_format = PCT
    ws.freeze_panes = "A2"

    s = LAST + 3
    t = ws.cell(row=s, column=1, value="Summary metrics — trailing 12 months (rows 26:37)")
    t.font = Font(bold=True, size=12, color="1F3864")
    ws.cell(row=s, column=1).border = THIN
    items = [
        ("S&M spend, last 12 months", f"=SUM(raw!F{W12}:F{LAST})", MONEY, False),
        ("New customers, last 12 months", f"=SUM(raw!C{W12}:C{LAST})", "#,##0", False),
        ("CAC (trailing 12 months)", f"=B{s+1}/B{s+2}", MONEY, True),
        ("Active customers (last month)", f"=F{LAST}", "#,##0", False),
        ("ARPA (last month MRR / active)", f"=raw!B{LAST}/F{LAST}", MONEY, True),
        ("Average gross margin, last 12 months", f"=AVERAGE(G{W12}:G{LAST})", PCT, False),
        ("Average monthly churn, last 12 months", f"=AVERAGE(H{W12}:H{LAST})", PCT, False),
        ("Gross profit per account per month", f"=B{s+5}*B{s+6}", MONEY, False),
        ("LTV (ARPA x avg GM / avg churn)", f"=B{s+5}*B{s+6}/B{s+7}", MONEY, True),
        ("LTV / CAC", f"=B{s+9}/B{s+3}", NUM, True),
        ("CAC payback (months)", f"=B{s+3}/(B{s+5}*B{s+6})", NUM, True),
        ("MRR (last month)", f"=raw!B{LAST}", MONEY, False),
        ("ARR (last month MRR x 12)", f"=raw!B{LAST}*12", MONEY, False),
        ("Revenue, last 12 months", f"=SUM(raw!B{W12}:B{LAST})", MONEY, False),
    ]
    for i, (label, formula, fmt, bold) in enumerate(items, start=1):
        _label(ws, s + i, label, formula, fmt, bold)
    ws.column_dimensions["A"].width = 38


def build_dcf(wb: Workbook):
    ws = wb.create_sheet("dcf")
    _title(ws, "DCF — 5-year unlevered free cash flow (no terminal value)")
    ws.column_dimensions["A"].width = 34
    for col in "BCDEFG":
        ws.column_dimensions[col].width = 16

    ws.cell(row=3, column=1, value="Assumptions").font = Font(bold=True, size=12, color="1F3864")
    _label(ws, 4, "Revenue year 0 (sum of last 12m MRR)", f"=SUM(raw!B{W12}:B{LAST})", MONEY)
    _label(ws, 5, "Discount rate", 0.12, PCT)
    _label(ws, 6, "Initial investment (year 0)", -5000000, MONEY)

    _header(ws, 8, ["Year"] + [f"Year {i}" for i in range(6)])
    for i, label in enumerate(["Revenue growth", "FCF margin"], start=9):
        ws.cell(row=i, column=1, value=label).font = Font(bold=True)
    for j, (g, m) in enumerate(zip([.25, .21, .17, .13, .10],
                                   [.15, .175, .20, .225, .25]), start=3):
        ws.cell(row=9, column=j, value=g).number_format = PCT
        ws.cell(row=10, column=j, value=m).number_format = PCT

    for row, label in ((12, "Revenue"), (13, "Free cash flow"), (14, "Net cash flow")):
        ws.cell(row=row, column=1, value=label).font = Font(bold=True)
    ws.cell(row=12, column=2, value="=B4").number_format = MONEY
    ws.cell(row=14, column=2, value="=B6").number_format = MONEY
    for j in range(3, 8):
        L, P = get_column_letter(j), get_column_letter(j - 1)
        ws.cell(row=12, column=j, value=f"={P}12*(1+{L}9)").number_format = MONEY
        ws.cell(row=13, column=j, value=f"={L}12*{L}10").number_format = MONEY
        ws.cell(row=14, column=j, value=f"={L}13").number_format = MONEY
    for j in range(2, 8):
        ws.cell(row=14, column=j).fill = BAND

    ws.cell(row=16, column=1, value="Valuation").font = Font(bold=True, size=12, color="1F3864")
    _label(ws, 17, "NPV @ discount rate", "=NPV(B5,C14:G14)+B14", MONEY, True)
    _label(ws, 18, "IRR", "=IRR(B14:G14)", PCT, True)
    _label(ws, 19, "Sum of undiscounted FCF (years 1-5)", "=SUM(C13:G13)", MONEY)


def build_loan(wb: Workbook):
    ws = wb.create_sheet("loan")
    _title(ws, "Loan — 2,000,000 at 7.00% annual, 60 equal monthly payments")
    ws.column_dimensions["A"].width = 34
    for col in "BCDEF":
        ws.column_dimensions[col].width = 18

    _label(ws, 3, "Principal", 2000000, MONEY)
    _label(ws, 4, "Annual interest rate", 0.07, PCT)
    _label(ws, 5, "Term (months)", 60, "#,##0")
    _label(ws, 6, "Monthly rate", "=B4/12", "0.0000%")
    _label(ws, 7, "Monthly payment", "=PMT(B6,B5,-B3)", MONEY, True)
    _label(ws, 8, "Total paid over term", "=B7*B5", MONEY)
    _label(ws, 9, "Total interest", "=SUM(D13:D72)", MONEY, True)
    _label(ws, 10, "Total principal repaid (check)", "=SUM(E13:E72)", MONEY)

    _header(ws, 12, ["Period", "Beginning balance", "Payment", "Interest",
                     "Principal", "Ending balance"])
    for i in range(60):
        r = 13 + i
        begin = "$B$3" if i == 0 else f"F{r - 1}"
        ws.cell(row=r, column=1, value=i + 1)
        ws.cell(row=r, column=2, value=f"={begin}")
        ws.cell(row=r, column=3, value="=$B$7")
        ws.cell(row=r, column=4, value=f"=B{r}*$B$6")
        ws.cell(row=r, column=5, value=f"=C{r}-D{r}")
        ws.cell(row=r, column=6, value=f"=B{r}-E{r}")
        for col in range(2, 7):
            ws.cell(row=r, column=col).number_format = MONEY
        if i % 2:
            for col in range(1, 7):
                ws.cell(row=r, column=col).fill = BAND
    ws.freeze_panes = "A13"


def main():
    wb = Workbook()
    wb.remove(wb.active)
    build_raw(wb, load_rows())
    build_unit_economics(wb)
    build_dcf(wb)
    build_loan(wb)
    OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    wb.save(OUT)
    print(f"wrote {OUT} sheets={wb.sheetnames}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values — touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe — run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure — do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job — magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). → `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) — each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. → `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette — run the script, don't reason about ΔE.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,…>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory — or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, ≥8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. → `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer — by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. → `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For ≥ 2 series a legend is always present and ≤ 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box — the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** — its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout — open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** — it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue — it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale → two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake — see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light→dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD ΔE ≥ 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6–8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL — full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead — see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view — it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for ≥ 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** — values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance — every value filled in — is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical — steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of — build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong — check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** — every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

def wrap(text, fnt, draw, max_w):
    lines, line = [], ""

    used = y - start
    if y > bottom - mb + 2:
        warnings.append(f"{label}: text overflows its box by {y - (bottom - mb)}px")
    return used


def draw_shape_fill(draw, shape, box):
    try:
        fill = shape.fill
        if fill.type is not None and fill.type == 1:
            colour = rgb(fill.fore_color, None)
            if colour:
                radius = min(18, (box[3] - box[1]) // 4) if "ROUNDED" in str(shape.shape_type) \
                    or (shape.has_text_frame and shape.height > Emu(0)) else 0
                if radius and box[2] - box[0] > 40 and box[3] - box[1] > 20:
                    draw.rounded_rectangle(box, radius=radius, fill=colour)
                else:
                    draw.rectangle(box, fill=colour)
    except Exception:
        pass


def draw_table(draw, shape, warnings, idx):
    tbl = shape.table
    x = px(shape.left)
    y = px(shape.top)
    widths = [px(c.width) for c in tbl.columns]
    heights = [px(r.height) for r in tbl.rows]
    for i, row in enumerate(tbl.rows):
        cx = x
        for j, cell in enumerate(tbl.cells(i) if hasattr(tbl, "cells") else
                                 [tbl.cell(i, j) for j in range(len(widths))]):
            box = (cx, y, cx + widths[j], y + heights[i])
            colour = rgb(cell.fill.fore_color, WHITE) if cell.fill.type == 1 else WHITE
            draw.rectangle(box, fill=colour, outline=(214, 222, 236))
            inner = (box[0] + px(cell.margin_left), box[1] + 4,
                     box[2] - px(cell.margin_right), box[3] - 4)
            used = draw_text_frame(draw, cell.text_frame, inner, [], "")
            if used > heights[i] - 4:
                warnings.append(f"slide {idx}: table cell ({i},{j}) text taller than its row")
            cx += widths[j]
        y += heights[i]


def render(pptx_path: Path, out_dir: Path):
    prs = Presentation(pptx_path)
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    W, H = px(prs.slide_width), px(prs.slide_height)
    warnings, paths = [], []
    for idx, slide in enumerate(prs.slides, start=1):
        img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), WHITE)
        draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
        for shape in slide.shapes:
            box = (px(shape.left), px(shape.top),
                   px(shape.left) + px(shape.width), px(shape.top) + px(shape.height))
            if shape.shape_type == MSO_SHAPE_TYPE.PICTURE:
                pic = Image.open(shape.image.blob and pptx_path.parent / "x" if False
                                 else __import__("io").BytesIO(shape.image.blob))
                img.paste(pic.convert("RGB").resize((box[2] - box[0], box[3] - box[1]),
                                                    Image.LANCZOS), (box[0], box[1]))
                continue
            if getattr(shape, "has_table", False) and shape.has_table:
                draw_table(draw, shape, warnings, idx)
                continue
            if shape.shape_type != MSO_SHAPE_TYPE.TEXT_BOX:
                draw_shape_fill(draw, shape, box)
            if shape.has_text_frame and shape.text_frame.text.strip():
                draw_text_frame(draw, shape.text_frame, box, warnings,
                                f"slide {idx} '{shape.text_frame.text[:34]}'")
            if box[0] < 0 or box[1] < 0 or box[2] > W + 1 or box[3] > H + 1:
                warnings.append(f"slide {idx}: shape extends past the slide edge {box}")
        path = out_dir / f"slide_{idx:02d}.png"
        img.save(path)
        paths.append(path)
    return paths, warnings


def main():
    src = Path(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "out/investor_update.pptx")
    paths, warnings = render(src, src.parent / "slides")
    print(f"rendered {len(paths)} slides -> {paths[0].parent}")
    print("\n".join(f"  ! {w}" for w in warnings) if warnings else "  no layout warnings")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
